clue.text: Postal worker reverses vehicle into stake — it is motorway strain

indicators.note: the vehicle named is said to reverse, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
a post is a stake driven into the ground
MI is the M1, Britain's first motorway
stress is strain

explanation.surface: A post office employee backs a bus into a fence post, and the motorway driving takes its toll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverses' turns BUS into SUB. 'into' and 'it is' only join the pieces. M1, often written MI in crosswords, is the London-to-Leeds motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: She runs a sub-post office, a small branch counter, so she is a postal worker.

clue.text: Second man's name for island

parts.note: Amos is a man's name, also an Old Testament prophet

explanation.surface: A second man gives his name to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Samos is a Greek island in the eastern Aegean.

clue.text: Invoice about changing a rate involving two sides

indicators.note: the invoice word goes round the other letters, as 'about' suggests

parts.note: a bill is an invoice

indicators.note: the words 'a rate' are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A bill disputes a changed rate agreed between two parties.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a billing dispute; 'about' wraps the invoice around the reshuffled letters, and 'involving two sides' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilateral means affecting or undertaken by two parties or sides.

clue.text: Duck has convulsive motion of the ear

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, the letter O
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A duck twitches its ear.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of zero in cricket, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is the anatomical adjective relating to hearing organs.

clue.text: Partial shaving of head is without doubt following the fashion

indicators.note: the word for certainty comes after the fashion word

parts.note: ton is an old word for the fashion or the fashionable set
sure means without doubt

explanation.surface: A trendy half-shaved head is certainly in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' just links. TON for fashion is a crossword staple from the French 'bon ton'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved crown of a monk or priest, a partial shave of the scalp.

clue.text: Tiny creatures appear in classes

parts.note: sects are groups or classes of believers

explanation.surface: Small animals turn up in school lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects are small six-legged creatures such as ants and beetles.

clue.text: Courts which provide refreshment during cases

indicators.note: the snack sits within the cases, as 'during' places one thing inside another

parts.note: trials are court cases
a bun is a light refreshment

explanation.surface: Courts that hand out snacks while hearing cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribunals are bodies that judge disputes, a kind of court.

clue.text: Insect we maybe meet in Minehead?

definitions.meaning: the dialect word in Somerset and Cornwall for a tourist, someone locals may meet at a seaside resort

explanation.surface: A bug you might come across at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: Minehead is a seaside resort in Somerset, where locals call both ants and visiting tourists by this dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmet is an old and dialect name for an ant, and West Country slang for a holidaymaker.

clue.text: Sits astride second Dicken's character

parts.note: Tommy Traddles is David Copperfield's friend in Dickens's novel

explanation.surface: A second Dickens character perches with legs on either side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicken's' is printed thus for Dickens's.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle something is to sit with one leg on each side of it.

clue.text: Ponder over Greek play for a division between lights

parts.note: to mull something over is to ponder it
Ion is a tragedy by Euripides

explanation.surface: Thinking over a Greek drama to find the dividing line between lamps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' just links. Lights here are window panes, not lamps.
explanation.definitionFit: A mullion is the vertical bar separating the panes of a window, which are called lights.

clue.text: Single man with me having right to glisten

parts.note: him is a man as object pronoun

explanation.surface: A bachelor and I, with justice on our side, gleam.
explanation.definitionFit: To shimmer is to shine with a wavering light, to glisten.

clue.text: Classes of saints about the east

indicators.note: the saints' letters go round the rest, as 'about' places them around

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
T' is the clipped dialect form of the definite article

explanation.surface: Groups of holy people circling the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SS around E and T, with T' the northern English 't'' for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sets are classes, as in school maths groups or groups of objects.

clue.text: Pointed play on words Trade Union acted awkwardly

parts.note: a pun is a play on words

indicators.note: the letters are arranged awkwardly, so they are shuffled

explanation.surface: A pun about trade unionists who performed clumsily, made pointedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' rearranges TU plus ACTED to give CTUATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointed, as in a written text, means marked with stops and commas.

clue.text: Caught divine revelation in boat

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an oracle is a message from the gods

explanation.surface: Someone receives a holy prophecy while in a little boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A coracle is a small round Welsh boat of wicker and hide.

clue.text: Map under order for special service troops

indicators.note: in a down clue the map letters sit below the order

parts.note: a command is an order
OS is Ordnance Survey, Britain's map makers

explanation.surface: Soldiers read a map under orders.
explanation.walkthrough: Ordnance Survey (OS) produces Britain's official maps.
explanation.definitionFit: Commandos are elite troops trained for raids, the special forces of wartime.

clue.text: One who puts questions about a chest it transforms

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: the letters of the words are transformed into a new order

explanation.surface: A questioner asks about a chest that changes shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transforms' rearranges A CHEST IT into ATECHIST, after C for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: A catechist teaches religion by question and answer.

clue.text: Skull the Spanish attached with small knife

parts.note: the scalp is the skin of the skull, taken as a trophy
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish skull found with a little blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attached with' just links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalpel is a small sharp surgical blade.

clue.text: Prerogative of having a member in what sounds like a lavatory

clue.text: Citizens army set new limit with one initial attack

indicators.note: the word limit is set in a new arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the initial letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A citizen army sets a new boundary and attacks first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set new' is the anagram signal on 'limit'; 'initial' takes just the first letter of 'attack'. A militia is drawn from ordinary citizens.
explanation.definitionFit: A militia is a force of ordinary citizens rather than regular soldiers.

clue.text: 7 down lifting a girl with its, feeler

parts.note: the answer at 7 down is a dialect word for an ant

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting turns the girl's name upward, so it reads backwards

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An ant raises a girl with its feeler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' turns ANNE upside down in the column, giving ENNA.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is an insect's feeler.

clue.text: Roman character caught fool in front of one American

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an ass is a fool
I is the Roman numeral for one
US stands for American, of the United States

explanation.surface: A Roman figure catches a fool ahead of a single American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in front of' just links the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassius is the conspirator against Caesar in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Picks mixed company with shoes

indicators.note: the letters are mixed into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone selects from a jumble of firms and footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges CO and SHOES together.
explanation.definitionFit: To choose is to pick or select.

clue.text: Share for note backing place

indicators.note: the note goes backwards, as backing suggests

parts.note: la is a note of the sol-fa scale
a location is a place

explanation.surface: A share in exchange for a note and a backing site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns LA into AL; 'for' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: An allocation is the portion or share allotted to someone.

clue.text: See monsieur embracing copper, the deputy

parts.note: lo is an old word for see or behold
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Look at the Frenchman hugging the policeman, the stand-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' puts CU inside M.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or priest standing in, a deputy.

clue.text: Man's direction to express disapproval

parts.note: his means belonging to a man
S, south, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A man's instructions on how to show displeasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Audiences hiss to show contempt or disapproval of a performer.

clue.text: It is agreeable for us in class

indicators.note: the pronoun goes in the class word

parts.note: a set is a class or group, as at school
we is the plural pronoun for us

explanation.surface: Being among our class is pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It is' and 'for' just link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet means pleasing or agreeable.

clue.text: Indian who is in the main, careful

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An Indian at sea who is careful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who is' links. The main is the open sea, a misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inca was a member of the Quechua people ruling Peru before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Speech from verdict I once delivered

indicators.note: the answer comes from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A speech delivered from a past verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivered' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Diction is the manner of speaking and enunciation.

clue.text: Pure incorporated in dry

indicators.note: the abbreviation for incorporated goes inside the word for dry

parts.note: sere means dry or withered

explanation.surface: Something pure included in dryness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means genuine, free of pretence, pure in feeling.

clue.text: Newspaper backing right answer dad finds not quite clear

parts.note: the Times is a newspaper
a dad is a parent

explanation.surface: Dad finds a newspaper's backing for the right answer unclear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns TIMES into SEMIT; 'finds' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Semitransparent means partly see-through, so not fully clear.
